subject: Cluster handoff: hardware mapping, storage split, and tenant isolation
content:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@stellabio.com>, Dan O'Neill <dan.oneill@stellabio.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Cluster handoff: hardware mapping, storage split, and tenant isolation

Hi Samantha / Dan,

Thanks for the intake call today. Per our discussion, attaching a short HW inventory template (hw_inventory_template.csv) — please fill in the rack/unit, NICs, NVMe/SSD counts, and BMC access. A couple of items we want to lock down early so we can finalize the Sprint Zero plan: 

- Node role proposals (we'll map to node pools): control-plane (3x), infra/egress (2x), inference GPU (as-needed), storage/replica nodes (2-3x depending on replication), and ephemeral workers.
- Storage strategy ask: do you want a distributed block store (Rook/Ceph or Longhorn) for persistent volumes, or do you prefer local PV + offsite backups? If you have a site preference, flag it.
- NVMe segregation: can we designate a separate NVMe pool for model cache vs. ephemeral scratch? We recommend isolating hot model cache to NVMe1 (dedicated) and use NVMe2/SSD for local ephemeral scratch.
- Encryption/KMS: confirm whether you'll provide a KMS endpoint (KMS hostname or HSM flow) or we should plan to use the platform's wrapped keys.
- Network: provide the site VPC/subnet CIDRs and any on-prem BGP peers/egress constraints.

Next steps: once we get the inventory + network diagram, we'll produce a node-pool mapping doc and a PVC/class proposal.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0199

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:14:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Cluster handoff: hardware mapping, storage split, and tenant isolation

Hi Marissa,

Thanks — attached is our initial inventory (hw_inventory_template_filled.csv). Quick answers inline: 

- We have two racks in Rack 12 with 4x NVMe per node (Samsung 3.84TB).
- We prefer local PVs for latency-sensitive model cache, and a lightweight distributed solution (Longhorn) for persistent metadata. Main concern is durability during power events — we have onsite backup windows.
- KMS: we have HashiCorp Vault with an internal transit endpoint (vault.stellabio.local) — we can provide a VPN endpoint and service account.
- Network: our infra team attached a simple diagram (site-network-drawings.png). BGP peer planned to the colo on 10.200.0.0/16.

Question: for Longhorn, will Redwood require dedicated storage nodes or can we use the infer nodes for both? We prefer to avoid extra chassis if possible.

Best,
Samantha

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha.li@stellabio.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cluster handoff: hardware mapping, storage split, and tenant isolation

Samantha — thanks for the inventory. A few recommendations based on what you provided: 

1) Node-pool mapping (proposed):
   - control-plane: 3x (small CPU, 64GB RAM) — tainted for control-plane only
   - infra/egress: 2x (dual 25G NICs, 128GB RAM) — handles routing, load balancing agents, and local cache proxies
   - inference-gpu: depending on model footprint, start with 4x A5000 (or equivalent) nodes, isolated via nodeSelector
   - storage-replica: 2x NVMe-heavy nodes (8x NVMe each) running Longhorn storage replicas OR Ceph OSD (if you pick Ceph)
   - worker-ephemeral: autoscaling worker pool for batch jobs and builds

2) Storage recommendation: 
   - For lowest token-ingest latency for model cache, use local PVs on NVMe1 (bindToLocalVolume). Persist model artifacts to the storage-replica pool asynchronously.
   - Longhorn is operationally simpler for small clusters and tolerates node restarts nicely, but Longhorn with NVMe on the same nodes as GPU can impact IO unless throttled. If you want predictable IO isolation, place Longhorn replicas on dedicated storage-replica nodes and reserve NVMe on inference nodes for local cache.

3) KMS and encryption: integrate Vault transit for envelope keys; we can use platform-side wrapping but Vault transit is preferred for key rotation and audit. Provide a service account and restricted CIDR for Vault API access.

4) Eviction and QoS: set eviction thresholds: imagefs.available <15% triggers eviction for non-critical pods; memory.available <10% for batch preemption. Use PodPriority classes for inference-critical workloads.

I'll bake these into a node-pool mapping doc and PVC class matrix.

—Karthik

-----
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Samantha Li <samantha.li@stellabio.com>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Cluster handoff: hardware mapping, storage split, and tenant isolation

Samantha / team — couple of clarifications on PVCs and encryption so the runbook is precise: 

- PVC AccessModes: model cache PVCs should be ReadWriteOnce and mounted only on inference nodes; metadata/backing stores can use ReadWriteMany if you run a distributed filesystem layer.
- Backup/restore: we need to define an RTO/RPO per tenant. For model cache (rebuildable), RPO can be larger; for training artifacts, RPO must be low and backups encrypted at rest.
- Node-level encryption: enable dm-crypt on NVMe devices with LUKS and use Vault to store LUKS keys. Plan for automated key rollout in the event of hardware replacement.
- Network egress: we should mark egress via infra nodes and set SNAT on the infra pool to contain outbound flows. This will help audits and limit external connections from worker nodes.

I'll add these as discrete checklist items in the Sprint Zero artifact.

Thanks,
Irene
